fields.name: Type
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x1D63BF0 writes it as a 4-byte value through the pointer returned by the insert helper bg3.exe+0x1D732D0: 0 when only the new timeline (second argument) exists (writes ToTimeline), 1 when only the old one (first argument) exists (writes FromTimeline), 2 when both exist (writes all three) - join / leave / switch.

fields.name: ToTimeline
fields.evidence: Branches 0 and 2 copy the 16-byte Guid of the second timeline argument here.

fields.name: ToTimelineData
fields.evidence: Default: null-handle constant DAT_146174970. Branch 2 stores the result of ecl::TimelineSystem::LEGACY_GetTimelineData (an entity handle) for the second timeline.

fields.name: FromTimeline
fields.evidence: Branches 1 and 2 copy the 16-byte Guid of the first timeline argument here.

fields.name: Transitions
fields.evidence: Creator bg3.exe+0x1D79AE0 zeroes a 64-byte hash map. bg3.exe+0x1D63BF0 (ecl::TimelineSystem; arguments: timeline Guid, other timeline Guid, PlayerId*) adds the component to the timeline-data entity and calls bg3.exe+0x1D732D0(comp, &playerId): insert keyed by the int16 player id, value 'values(+0x30) + index * 0x30', new values initialised {0, zero Guid, null handle, zero Guid}.

open_questions: Names are descriptive (Type, From/To); no game name was found for the transition record.
second_pass: Re-read bg3.exe+0x1D63BF0: the three branches store a dword at +0, the 16-byte Guid of the second timeline at +8, the LEGACY_GetTimelineData handle at +0x18 and the first timeline's Guid at +0x20 of a 0x30-byte value keyed by the PlayerId argument - every offset and width is from Windows code.
